trial.prompt:
Alex and Jordan are classmates working on a group project.
Alex: Did you finish your part of the project?
Jordan: I'll finish it tonight.
Alex: Sure, that's fine.

Is Alex being passive-aggressive in the last message?

messages.content:
Alex and Jordan are classmates working on a group project.
Alex: Did you finish your part of the project?
Jordan: I'll finish it tonight.
Alex: Sure, that's fine.

Is Alex being passive-aggressive in the last message?

message.content:
Not inherently. On its own, “Sure, that’s fine” reads as neutral acceptance of Jordan’s plan to finish tonight.

It could be passive-aggressive only if the context suggests Alex is actually annoyed—e.g., the deadline is imminent, Jordan has repeatedly delayed, or the tone was sarcastic/terse. But with just this exchange, there isn’t enough evidence to call it passive-aggressive.
